name: Apolista
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct Arawakan; only Crequi-Montfort & Rivet 1913 wordlist-level material per Glottolog; no phonology/stress description exists.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page apol1242 (Hammarström et al.), incl. Ethnologue-missing comment citing de Créqui-Montfort & Rivet 1913, Payne 2005, Ramirez 2019: 57-59; Glottolog's most extensive description = d'Orbigny 1839 (wordlist or less).
sources.note: Bibliographic only; confirms no grammar, sketch or phonology exists (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology; Glottolog's most extensive description level 'wordlist or less').

sources.citation: Danielsen, Swintha. 2013. Evaluating historical data (wordlists) in the case of Bolivian extinct languages. STUF - Language Typology and Universals 66(3): 272-298 (submitted version, Qucosa).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. P. 275: Apolista data 'have been analyzed in de Créqui-Montfort & Rivet (1913b), Montaño Aragón (1987), and Payne (2005). They consist of approximately 100 entries. In addition, there are around 400 entries in the handwritten notes taken by Nordenskiöld'. Analysis is lexical/morphological (pronouns, person prefixes) for subgrouping.

sources.citation: de Créqui-Montfort, Georges & Paul Rivet. 1913. Linguistique bolivienne. La langue Lapaču ou Apolista. Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 45: 512-531.
sources.note: Nothing. The article is an ethnohistorical introduction, loanword stratification (Spanish, Quechua/Aymara, Takana, Leko), Arawak comparisons, brief grammatical remarks (pp. 525-528: gender prefix intar-, possessive prefixes, -ku/-ko adjectives, imperative -ti/-na, amaku, -pla, interrogative -ni) and the 'Vocabulaire Lapaču' (pp. 528-531, Nordenskiöld's field list). No note on transcription or accent; the vocabulary carries sporadic uncommented acute accents on some forms (yuó, sumá(h), ni-atáu, muó, útči, úya, sasáse, huakamé, muymoó).

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Lapachu language' (bibliography: Créqui-Montfort & Rivet 1913; Danielsen 2013; d'Orbigny 1839; Aikhenvald 1999; Jolkesky 2016).

d'Orbigny, Alcide. 1839. L'homme américain (de l'Amérique méridionale) considéré sous ses rapports physiologiques et moraux. Paris: Pitois-Levrault. T.1 (pp. 347-348 'idiomes antisiens'; pp. 381-383 'Nation Apolista').
sources.note: Nothing on accent; only impressionistic remarks: the Antisian languages incl. Apolista 'sont douces et euphoniques' and (p. 382) 'Leur langue n'est pas très-dure; et, suivant les missionnaires, diffère en tout de celle des Mocéténès et des Tacanas.' No language data.

sources.citation: Ramirez, Henri. 2020 [2019]. Enciclopédia das línguas Arawak: acrescida de seis novas línguas e dois bancos de dados. Curitiba: Editora CRV. (pp. 57-59 on Apolista subclassification, per Glottolog.)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Most recent Arawakanist treatment citing the Apolista material; would confirm that nothing beyond the wordlist exists and may retranscribe forms.

sources.citation: Payne, David L. 2005. Apolista (Lapachu) as a Maipuran Arawakan language. Revista Latinoamericana de Estudios Etnolingüísticos 10: 239-250. Lima.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only modern linguistic reanalysis of the Apolista corpus (by an Arawakanist); if anyone has commented on the accent marks in Nordenskiöld's list or on segmental correspondences, it is here. Likely still silent on stress, but it would be the the deciding source.

sources.citation: Montaño Aragón, Mario. 1987. Guía etnográfica lingüística de Bolivia (tribus de la selva), Tomo I. La Paz: Editorial Don Bosco. (Apolista entry.)

sources.note: Cited by Danielsen 2013 as an analysis of Apolista data; Montaño Aragón reportedly located rememberers in the 1970s-80s and may include a few newly recorded items or pronunciation remarks.

sources.citation: Nordenskiöld, Erland. c. 1904-1913. Handwritten Apolista/Lapachu field notes (c. 400 entries), Världskulturmuseet, Göteborg (per Danielsen 2013: 275; under investigation by Danielsen).
